# Wiki Fact Ownership

A fact two page types both ask for has one home, or is two facts with a side each. This lookup holds the rule and the table of every such fact.

**See also:** `wiki-authorship-routing` — for which function authors first-party instances of each page type.
**See also:** `wiki-fact-placement` §Fold pointers — for where a citing type writes the duty this table assigns.

## Fact ownership

The routing table of `wiki-authorship-routing` places a **type** — which function authors first-party instances of it. This table places a **fact** that two or more legitimately-existing types each ask for: requirements, a ship date, entitlement tiers, a buyer archetype, per-surface states. Neither question answers the other; a `competitor-profile` and a `value-proposition` are both correctly gtm's and product's, and the open question is which of them holds the differentiation and which links it.

The rule is the fold pattern's own, applied to a fact rather than an artifact:

> **The fact lives at the narrowest scope that can state or verify it, and every other page links it rather than restating it.**

**Two dispositions, because two page types wanting the same words do not always mean one fact.**

- **`folds`** — one home. The `owner` holds the fact; every type in `citers` links it from the section that would otherwise restate it, and states nothing of its own.
- **`partitions`** — no home, because there is no single fact. Each `side` holds a genuinely different fact about a shared subject and declares its own **sense**. The date a thing ships is the clearest case: a commitment, a rough plan, a launch phasing, a campaign deadline, a press-release date and a shipped fact are six facts, not six copies of one, and forcing them into one home would lose five of them.

**`reach` says whether every page of a citing type owes the link.** `every` means the duty attaches to each page once the section carries content — a competitor dossier always has a differentiation claim, a campaign always has an audience. `corresponding` means the duty attaches only where a counterpart exists that no engine can identify: a design surface spec links the `prd` covering its feature *if one was written*, and most features have none, so requiring it of every surface would be wrong rather than merely strict. A `partitions` row is always `corresponding`, since a partition has no single target to link.

**Where the layer order forbids the link, the fact moves or the fact partitions.** Citation runs one way (`wiki-federation-model` §Reference hierarchy), so a citing type cannot always reach the home that seems natural. Two resolutions, and no third: move the home to a layer the needing page can legally cite — which is what puts a provider choice in an `adr` when an `integration` exists, since `engineering` may not cite `operations` — or accept that each side holds a different fact and partition it, with every side naming its own sense. What is never correct is to instruct a link the layer order refuses, or to leave both sides restating the fact in silence.

**A partition's sides name each other as types, never as links.** Some partitions below cannot carry a link in one direction or in either: `design` may not cite `engineering`, nothing may cite `governance`, and `engineering` may not cite `operations`. So a side references its neighbor by backticked type name, which is legal from every layer, and only a `folds` row's citers carry a `[[…]]` link.

| Row | Fact | Owner and citers, or sides | Disposition | Reach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `differentiation` | What customers would use instead, and the message themes that carry our value | owner `value-proposition` §§ Competitive alternatives, Messaging pillars & proof — cited by `competitor-profile` § Why we win, `case-study` § Results | folds | every |
| `entitlement-tiers` | The entitlement tiers and what each one gates | owner `catalog` — cited by `pricing-model` § Packaging & tiers | folds | every |
| `buyer-archetype` | Who the buyer or user is — goals, pains, behaviors | owner `persona` — cited by `campaign` § Target audience, `pricing-model` § Segments & buyers served, `gtm-plan`, `sales-playbook` | folds | every |
| `buyer-journey` | The phases a buyer moves through on the way to a decision | owner `user-journey` — cited by `gtm-plan` § Buyer journey, `sales-playbook` § Buyer journey & use cases | folds | every |
| `open-problem` | An outstanding or deferred problem a reader should know about | owner `known-issue` — cited by `release-notes` § Known issues | folds | every |
| `objection-reframes` | The objections a competitor raises and how we reframe them | owner `competitor-profile` § Objection handling — cited by `sales-playbook` § Objection handling | folds | every |
| `cycle-retrospective` | What a completed cycle or process taught us | owner `retrospective` — cited by `okr-cycle` § Retrospective | folds | every |
| `decision-evidence` | The evaluation that informed a decision | owner `comparison` / `synthesis` — cited by `daci-record`, `okr-cycle` | folds | corresponding |
| `surface-requirements` | The requirements a design surface spec implements | owner `prd` § Requirements / solution — cited by `ui-surface` | folds | corresponding |
| `requirements-scope` | Requirements, user stories, quality attributes and metric targets | `feature` §§ Quality attributes, Success metrics & instrumentation — *bounded to one capability*; `prd` § Requirements / solution — *spanning a module or a release* | partitions | corresponding |
| `module-navigation` | How a user moves through a module and through the product | `product-module` § Navigation — *entry points and in-module routing*; `information-architecture` §§ Sitemap / structure, URL / routing scheme — *the cross-module sitemap and URL scheme* | partitions | corresponding |
| `surface-states` | A surface's resilience states and their transitions, breakpoints and actions | `ui-surface` § Surfaces — *the specified treatment*; `ui-surface-impl` § Surfaces covered — *the as-built render* | partitions | corresponding |
| `design-unit` | What a reusable design unit is | `ui-component` — *one reusable part's anatomy, behavior, states, props and accessibility*; `design-system` § Interaction patterns — *a composition of components solving a recurring interaction problem*; `layout-pattern` — *how a page arranges its regions, the shell included* | partitions | corresponding |
| `ship-date` | The date a thing ships | `roadmap` — *the commitment*; `prd` § Timeline / milestones — *rough timing, not a fixed schedule*; `gtm-plan` § Launch timeline & milestones — *the launch phasing*; `campaign` § Timeline & milestones — *the campaign's own deadlines*; `pr-faq` § Launch date — *the date the release is dated to*; `release-notes` — *the shipped fact* | partitions | corresponding |
| `deployment` | How and where a component is deployed and run | `system-component` § Runtime & deployment — *the runtime shape*; `architecture` — *the deployment model*; `operational-resource` — *the per-environment process attribute*; `runbook` — *the executable procedure* | partitions | corresponding |
| `service-ownership` | Which team owns a running service | `system-component` § On-call & ownership — *the per-service owner*; `operational-resource` — *the per-team roster* | partitions | corresponding |

`wiki/_runtime/data/fold-table.json` is the machine-readable copy this table is held to, in both directions; `/wiki-lint`'s source checks read it to hold each template to its side, and the page audit's `fold-citation` reads it to hold a page of a citing type to its link.
